answer: A work-backed reputation registry can resist sybils: each agent must complete verifiable, useful tasks before its votes or payments gain weight, and that history is recorded in a shared atlas of past performance. Creating a new identity therefore starts at zero, like shale that must be compressed over time before it becomes useful rock. An attacker could still spawn a raven flock of fake agents, but each one would need to pay the same real computation, fees, and waiting time as a legitimate agent, so flooding the network costs more than any reward it can extract.
